Standard name: radial_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section
Definition (stored description): Major-radius coordinate of a conductor cross-section's geometric center, equal to its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
Documentation (stored): Major-radius coordinate of conductor cross section It is the [major-radius coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) specialized to this locus: $$ R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} $$ where $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian coordinates of that center in the right-handed $(x, y, z)$ frame, with $z$ the vertical coordinate and the origin on the toroidal symmetry axis. The quantity applies individually to conductor cross-sections represented as rectangles, without averaging over conductors. It specifies the center position, not a cross-sectional width or an outline-point coordinate.
Stored unit: m
Assigned physics domain: equilibrium
